newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB policy unchanged despite firm money rates.
newsitem.headline: SNB policy unchanged despite firm money rates.

text.p: Recent tightness in Swiss money markets is not a result of any policy shift by the Swiss National Bank (SNB), an SNB spokesman said in response to an enquiry.

Asked whether it was correct that the latest tightness in money market rates was technical, the spokesman said "From our point of view, that is entirely accurate. There hasn't been any change in the policy stance."
"It does happen...when the currency moves in one direction, that interest rates move in the other direction," the spokesman added.
He also noted that Swiss short-term interest rates can move at times independent of monetary policy.
The SNB does not target a precise short-term interest rate but rather, sets its long-term policy based on monetary targets.
"Rates do fluctuate in our system. It is not a system that sets one rate in a fixed way," the spokesman said.

Money market traders noted earlier Wednesday that Swiss short-term rates, including tomorrow/next money, have lately risen above 1-1/2 percent. In late September, rates tended at times to trade closer to 1-3/8 percent. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
